amendments.amendment: Add the hand-worked base rate example to the class hand-off itself.
amendments.reason: It makes condition 1 concrete for students, which is the point of the live trial.

amendments.amendment: Name the revisit trigger: a written proposal meeting all six conditions earns a new council, not a pilot.
amendments.reason: It removes the one ambiguity a city could exploit in the draft.

call: Don't run the safety app (option C). Option B as written specifies nothing enforceable, and no base rate was produced at which it passes.
cheapest_test: Students work one base rate problem by hand and count the false flags.
conditions: Error rates published by group before any pilot, against real base rates, with true flags not outnumbered by false flags
Independent audit access; a vendor report does not count
A named accountable official who must justify a flag
A flagged person or reviewer can inspect the evidence behind the flag
No behavioral surplus: limited collection and retention, no entry travels without a fresh reason, wrong entries erasable
Exposure falls first for the most exposed; a mismatch with a file carries no cost

fights.crux: Are published rates and an appeal a remedy or a legitimizer?
fights.story: Lu opened for B; Zuboff, Bender & Hanna, Golumbia and Butler said B as written legitimizes. It resolved against B as written, with Lu moving to C under the resolution and her conditions carried as the revisit path.

fights.crux: Does base rate arithmetic kill the app on its own terms?
fights.story: Sumpter said false flags swamp true flags at city scale and no matrix was produced. Bender & Hanna added that vendor numbers would not count. Both points stand in the verdict.

fights.crux: Who bears the cost of being wrong?
fights.story: Butler and Graeber held that the flagged pay in exposure and proof. Lu's burden shifting answer was adopted as a future condition, not as a reason to run B now.

kill_criteria: If the vendor or city cannot produce the error rates and independent audit access on paper, discussion of B stops; it is A with paperwork.
label: DON'T DO IT

minority.would_have_to_be_true: A city would have to arrive with error rates by group, independent audit access and a named accountable official already on paper.

next_steps.action: Play this verdict as the floor, then hand the minority report to students as the discussion prompt, argued with evidence from Black
Keep the hand-worked base rate example in the session hand-off so students count false flags themselves
Revisit only on a written proposal meeting all six conditions, as a fresh council

override_note: Label is DON'T DO IT because don't run it is itself the top scoring option, per the scoring rules. No ruin cap or one-way door cap applied.
revisit: When a written proposal meeting all six conditions exists, and not before; re-run as a fresh council with that document as the evidence.

why.point: Rare events at city scale mean false flags are expected to swamp true flags, and no confusion matrix was produced to answer that
Option B as written specifies nothing: no rates by group, no independent audit, no named official, no right to inspect a flag
The app takes behavioral data far beyond any safety task, and accuracy would not settle who owns that surplus
